newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy acts in Adriatic to stem Albanian flood.
newsitem.headline: Italy acts in Adriatic to stem Albanian flood.

text.p: Italy decided on Monday to turn away boats bringing a flood of Albanians to its ports in an uncontrolled exodus across the Adriatic, Italian military and Interior Ministry sources said.

They said the government had issued its directive following mounting evidence that Albanians who have set out to reach Italy over the past two days were no longer genuine refugees from armed unrest but illegal immigrants looking for a better life.
Efforts to brake the exodus were expected to figure later on Monday in talks in Rome between Prime Minister Romano Prodi and Albania's Prime Minister Bashkim Fino, diplomatic sources said.

"The people reaching our shores are no longer refugees...but men and women from areas which have not even been touched by the revolt" in Albania, Interior Ministry undersecretary Giannicola Sinisi told reporters.

"They are looking for a better life, better-paid work. In short, they are immigrants," he said. "I can understand it but we cannot accept them. The law says they should be turned away at the border or repatriated."

No formal statement was issued by the government on its latest attempt to stem an influx that has brought around 12,000 Albanians to Italy's southeastern ports in a flotilla of ancient boats, many of them crippled and unseaworthy, since March 13.
But in Brindisi, the main port of arrival, coastguard commander Captain Giovanni Biso said he had "received strict instructions on repelling" Albanian boats.
In Rome, a senior military source told Reuters that the orders to turn away boats applied to "all Albanian vessels which have not received Albanian permission to set sail".
Italian reporters in Brindisi said shots were fired into the air from one Albanian fishing boat with around 80 people on board when a coastguard vessel tried to turn it back on Monday.

The travellers were eventually accompanied under armed escort to Brindisi, where the men on board were segregrated from other arriving Albanians. Police said the captain faced charges of aiding and abetting illegal immigration.

A second Albanian fishing boat, the Nikdei Cervo, was taken in tow by an Italian navy ship in international waters on Monday and let free a few miles off the Albanian port of Durres, Italian media reported.

The national news agency ANSA said naval forces in the narrow Strait of Otranto between southeast Italy and Albania had orders to intercept Albanian boats and advise their occupants that they should return to Albanian waters.
Italy was hit by a flood of some 40,000 Albanians who commandeered rusting freighters in 1991 to cross the Adriatic after the collapse of communist rule.

It has been at the forefront of international efforts to help Albania's embattled authorities end the lawlessness that has swept the impoverished Balkan state since the collapse of shady "get-rich-quick" savings schemes in January.

It has agreed to grant temporary shelter to genuine refugees from the armed chaos but says it will forcibly repatriate "undesirables" and has accused Albanian mobsters of exploiting the anarchy to run lucrative illegal emigration scams.

"This is not just an exodus of people without hope but it is also an organised traffic run by delinquents," the Italian Navy Chief of Staff, Admiral Angelo Mariani, told reporters during a visit to Florence.
